turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's essay. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be direct: you gave him a zero and nobody called me first. What do you have?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"The end of it." Okay. The company that sells that checker says its number shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student, and your own procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern. What else do you have?
I don't need more proof than that.
"Don't need more." Okay. Procedure 4.2 says you call the parent before any mark goes in, and 4.1 says you speak to the student first. Did you do either, Hale?
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
"Unlike some people." I'm writing that down. My son doesn't lie, so are you calling him a liar, or me?

"Zero stands." Okay. No call to me, no conversation with Owen, and a score the vendor says not to rely on alone. I'll be in the principal's office when we're done here, so last chance, Hale: what else do you have?
